key_insight: In a localized nonorthogonal flow representation, Reynolds stress comes from coupled velocity fluctuations, so separate structure energies cannot capture its assembly.
engineering_relevance: Structure-based turbulence analysis must retain overlap and cross covariance to avoid misleading momentum-flux attribution.
method: Represent JHTDB homogeneous isotropic turbulence using a frozen solenoidal expansion of curl-lifted anisotropic Gaussian vorticity functions.
Measure blob-, sheet-, and tube-like velocity-span overlap using principal angles and self-cross covariance.
Compare stress assembly with orthogonal Fourier and POD regroupings of the same velocity.
evidence_signal: At a principal cosine of 0.95, 55% of sheet-associated directions overlap closely with tube-like directions; shared-direction products carry 99.6% of covariance cancellation, and removing between-family covariance raises DNS-referenced stress error by factors of 53.6–87.
watch_item: Morphology labels and stress attribution are representation-dependent; these results do not establish unique physical contributions from named structures.
paper_title: Identifiability Limits of Reynolds-Stress Attribution in Localized Nonorthogonal Flow Representations
